brief: A kitchen herb planter: two or three bins on a base, filled with soil and planted with basil and thyme.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Two or three bins on a base
requirements.evidence: 3 bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) connected in L-shape with jointBolts, each holding a bin: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full — total 3 bins within requested 2-3 range.
All three bins filled to rim: soil entries for bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full via fillSoil.
Planted: prop:1 basil-young in bin:0,0,0, prop:2 thyme-young in bin:0,1,0, prop:3 basil-harvest in bin:1,0,0 — both requested herb species present, visible in look views (az45/polar62 and top-down).

finish.summary: Built L-shaped kitchen herb planter with 3 bases and 3 full-depth bins, all filled with soil and planted with basil (young + harvest) and thyme (young). Caps and joint bolts applied, mesh clear, all plants visible from above and side.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Herb garden coming up — I'll set a base with soil-filled bins for your basil and thyme.
